title: Gaps and Opportunities in Death Certification and Mortality Reporting Systems in Libya
content: Background: Accurate death certification and mortality reporting are essential components of functional Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) systems and are critical for evidence-based public health decision-making. However, many low- and middle-income countries face challenges in ensuring completeness and quality of mortality data.Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using a structured document and system analysis approach. National documents, legal frameworks, reporting forms, and institutional reports related to death certification and mortality reporting in Libya were systematically identified through database searches, institutional repositories, and consultation with stakeholders. Data were analysed using a framework aligned with World Health Organization standards for CRVS systems.Results: A total of 38 documents published between 1968 and 2026 were included. Findings revealed gaps in the availability, dissemination and standardisation of national guidelines, limited alignment with international death certification standards, and fragmentation in mortality reporting systems. Challenges included inconsistent use of standard cause-of-death certification and limited integration between institutions.Conclusion: Libya has made significant progress in improving its CRVS. Yet, considerable gaps still exist in death certification and mortality reporting systems in Libya. Strengthening and dissemination of national guidelines, improving system integration, and aligning with international standards are critical to enhancing mortality data quality.
